name: GitHub
description: Manage GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, and Actions in Cindy. When you open a PR, an interactive card helps you submit it and automatically follows CI and reviews until merge. Uses the local GitHub login. Supports github.com.
whenToUse: Use for github.com repositories and links; use GitLab for GitLab instances. Handles issues, PRs, reviews, merges, repositories, Actions, releases, search, and logs. Use the PR card to ask about opening a PR and to show its status afterwards. Uses the local GitHub login or a fallback token.

list_tools.description: List this plugin's 117 GitHub operations across issues, pulls, repo, commits, actions, releases, search, users, orgs, events, notifications, gists, git_data, reactions, and meta. With no category, return category names, counts, and descriptions; with a category, return every operation in that category with its description and parameters.

call_tool.description: Run a GitHub operation returned by list_tools, passing args according to its parameter schema. Repository operations require explicit owner and repo values, which may be derived from git remote get-url origin when working in a repository. API-link fields are removed by default except html_url; set raw=true for the original JSON. Results over 50KB are written to the session work directory and only the file path is returned; out_file can set the path. Downloads such as Actions artifacts or log ZIPs require a destination directory in the top-level save_dir field of ghost_call.

pr_card.description: Show a PR card in Cindy. Before publishing, pass repo, head and base, optionally with commits and files. After this task successfully publishes, pass published=true and pr, plus card_id if available. On supported hosts the card starts follow-up for a non-draft PR when the saved setting is enabled. Pass following=false if the user asked to publish only. Omit published when viewing an existing PR. If follow_state is present, the card owns follow-up and you must not create another schedule. active means running, paused means paused, stopped means ended, failed means setup failed, and unverified means the state could not be confirmed. On older hosts, use todo only when follow_state is absent. Before creating a schedule yourself, pass claim_follow=true and require follow_claimed=true. existing_task points to the task already responsible, and the card link only navigates there. Report only verified operations via renamed and following. Refresh via card_id and use to_latest when notifying.

pr_follow_settings.description: Read the same auto-rename, auto-follow and follow-model preferences used by PR cards. Returns settings without showing a card, creating a task or starting follow-up; preferences are not proof that following is active. Use after opening a PR in IM too, then create and verify follow-up with the pr workflow. A read failure means unknown, not disabled.

status_watch.description: Manage local GitHub status watches; add only when explicitly asked. Specify owner/repo, pr / issue / run and PR, issue or Actions run ID. remove stops, list shows. Polls five targets every five minutes; notifies only changes. list returns kind, repo, id, status, problem. pr/issue status is `state:draft:comments`: state in open/closed/merged, draft in draft/ready, last segment the comment count. run status is `state:conclusion:attempt`: state in queued/requested/waiting/pending/in_progress/completed, conclusion none until completion then success/failure/cancelled/neutral/skipped/timed_out/action_required/stale/startup_failure/unknown, last segment the run attempt. problem is null when healthy. unavailable clears on the next successful read. account_changed means the host GitHub account switched and this watch is paused; it resumes when the account matches again, or remove then add to watch under the new account. target_changed means the object identity changed; it never clears on its own, so remove then add.
